NONE: › one of the smaller groups or amounts that a larger group or amount can be divided into
（群體或事物的）部分
› mathematics part of a circle that is divided from the rest by a line, or part of a sphere that is divided from the rest by two planes
弓形，圓缺，球缺
› one of the small parts that a fruit such as an orange is naturally divided into
（水果）瓣
› a short piece of film that forms part of a television or radio programme, or that is broadcast on the internet
（電視、廣播或互聯網節目的）節，段
› to divide something into different parts
分離；分割

example: People over the age of 85 make up the fastest-growing segment of the population.
85歲以上者成爲人口增長最快的部分。
Each of these products is aimed at a specific market segment.
每一種產品針對的都是市場的不同部分。
The salad was decorated with segments of orange.
CNN last week broadcast a segment on homicides in the city.
CNN上周播出了有關這座城市兇殺狀況節目的一段。
The market is segmented by price into three general categories.
根據價格將市場大體分為三類。

NONE: › relating to or forming segments or parts
節段的；分段的；部分的
› to keep one group of people apart from another and treat them differently, especially because of race or sex
（尤指基於種族或性別原因）隔離並差別對待
› to keep one thing separate from another
分離；分開

example: 實行種族隔離的學校／社會
Blacks were segregated from whites in every area of life.
在生活中的各方各面，黑人和白人被隔離開。
The systems will have to be able to segregate clients' money from the firm's own cash.
該系統必須能夠把客戶的錢同公司的自有資金分開。

流暢地轉換
